The 36 active invariants declare expected proof tiers at the compiler pin. The proof gate checks compiler-owned dependency edges, proof status, tier and qualifiers, satisfying and corrupt controls, and non-vacuous preconditions. models.notes: Flagship transcendental pricer. bs_call_scalar wraps the pure-f64 bs_call_f64 (both exported); the shipped Greeks differentiate bs_call_f64.
Black-76 forward call. Shares the lognormal european-call invariant family with bs_call, so the same kind-level invariants instantiate against a second model (kind-reuse demonstration).

Closed-form 2-step CRR European call. Pure arithmetic + ITE (no transcendentals), so its pricing structure lowers to cvc5 -- the shell's genuine proven-over-reals model. General-depth CRR needs induction and is held out.

DEFECTIVE reference model (sprint in-region-break deliverable). Identical to tr_crr_call_2step but with the discount factor DROPPED -- it returns the raw risk-neutral expected payoff, not its present value (a real, common finance bug: forgetting to discount). It conforms to the european_call_fixed_depth kind yet VIOLATES the no-arbitrage upper bound C <= s inside its valid input region (verified in-domain witness s=1.0 k=0.5 u=2.0 d=0.5 q=0.5 gives price 1.125 > spot 1.0). See invariant shoals.inv.call_upper_bounded_by_spot.crr_nodisc_defect.v1.

Risk-neutral 2-step CRR European call: the per-step discount is DERIVED as disc = 1/(q*u+(1-q)*d), so the discounted underlying is a martingale by construction (no-arbitrage-consistent). Pure arithmetic + division + ITE, lowers to cvc5. The genuine proven-over-reals ANCHOR for the model-free european_call no-arbitrage canon (nonneg, upper bound C<=s, intrinsic lower bound, bull spread, butterfly). The value bounds hold ONLY under the martingale condition, so they FAIL on the free-parameter tr_crr_call_2step (which admits an in-domain arbitrage witness) -- that contrast is the teaching exemplar of genuine-vs-deferred.
Closed-form 2-period discount factor 1/(1+y)^2. Pure arithmetic + division, lowers to cvc5. Anchors the discount-factor-bounded invariant (in (0,1] for y >= 0).

Closed-form 2-period unit-face coupon bond PV = c/(1+y) + (1+c)/(1+y)^2. Pure arithmetic + division, lowers to cvc5 -- the genuine proven-over-reals rates anchor (bond PV bounds, price-yield monotonicity, convexity). Held at n=2: the three-point convexity second difference over reciprocal powers is unsupported at n>=3 at this pin, so a 2-period bond is the largest schedule that proves d2P/dy2>0 in the faithful yield form. General-schedule discounting needs a fold (no induction tier at 0.16.1) and is held out.

DEFECTIVE reference model (sprint in-region-break deliverable, rates analogue of tr_crr_call_2step_nodisc). Identical cashflows to fi_bond2 but summed with NO discounting -- returns the nominal sum c+(1+c) and ignores the yield, a real and common rates bug. It conforms to the coupon_bond kind yet VIOLATES strict price-yield monotonicity inside its valid region (its price is constant in y, so DV01/duration is understated to zero). See invariant shoals.inv.fi_bond_pv_monotone_in_yield.nodisc_defect.v1.
Parametric (Gaussian) VaR: mu + sigma * Phi^{-1}(alpha). Uses normal_inv_cdf, so its active coherence invariants are separately fuzz-validated against the real parametric body.

Historical VaR delegates to Nautilus.Stats.quantile_vec. Its coherence family is observed separately from the Gaussian inverse-CDF family, with compiler-owned edges to the real historical_var and historical_cvar declarations.
